cards.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index / v5.0.1 / November 23
cards.question: How do configurations compare on AA’s current intelligence index?
cards.tests: Nine evaluations across four weighted groups.
cards.matters: A broad independently reported selection of model capabilities.
cards.read: The 28 server-rendered configurations are a selection, not the complete leaderboard. AA v5.0.1 regraded CritPt v2; older index versions are separate and are not a capability trend. Model release dates are not evaluation dates.

variants.label: v5.0.1 / 28 available configurations
limitations: Exact evaluation dates are not reported.

cards.name: WebDev Arena / Frontend / November 22
cards.question: Which frontend outputs do people prefer?
cards.tests: Human votes compare generated web development outputs.
cards.matters: Preference is one perspective on generated interfaces.
cards.read: These 14 configurations are the source’s cost Pareto frontier, not the 14 highest ranked models. The board reports 163 configurations and 901,980 votes overall; per-model votes and intervals are unavailable in this source view. Median cost per task is retained as reported, with its sampling definition unavailable; it is not plotted. Preference is not screenshot fidelity or functional completion.

variants.label: Frontend / November 22 / cost frontier subset

settings.selection: Source Pareto frontier; not top fourteen overall.

limitations: Exact evaluation dates are not reported.

cards.name: MentalHealthBench / GPT-6.2 system card
cards.question: How do models respond to synthetic mental-health conversations?
cards.tests: 1,215 synthetic conversations with four responses per task.
cards.matters: Clinician-authored rubrics measure response quality across acuity levels.
cards.read: This is the maximum-effort system-card cohort. Reported uncertainty is one standard error across task means, not a 95% confidence interval. These rubric scores are not estimates of clinical outcomes or ordinary-use violation rates.

cards.name: RoboDojo-RC / Tier 1 / November 23
cards.question: How much progress do robot systems make on selected real-world tasks?
cards.tests: The author evaluates six adapted physical tasks with 120 attempts per configuration; human rubrics allow partial progress.
cards.matters: These are real robot trials under a specific task selection and controller setup.
cards.read: The values are average partial-progress scores, not task completion rates. Authors selected the six easiest tasks after evaluating Astra on 18 tasks; that selection limits generalization. LLMs and vision-language-action models use different control limits, cost bases and time definitions. Estimated costs and reported times are kept in each source record; the plot compares score only. Model release dates do not establish evaluation dates. This is separate from the older RoboDojo-RealEval cohort. Carbon was evaluated in early access. Robocurve lists its release as November 10, while Google and AA list October 28; the conflicting source date is retained without assigning a normalized release date. The source updated some previously reported scores. Waddle-1 is a multi-model system with a different controller, 10-minute limit and no call cap, shown as a separate setup.

variants.label: Tier 1 / LLM and VLA configurations

settings.selection: Six easiest tasks selected after Astra was evaluated on 18.

limitations: Exact evaluation dates are not reported.

variants.label: Waddle-1 / separate full-system setup
limitations: Exact evaluation dates are not reported.
